   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e3ef70a2",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Importing data from Eyelink ASC files\n",
    "\n",
    "This example shows how to read `.asc` files generated from Eyelink EDF files using `edf2asc`. Usually, it is easier to read the EDF file directly, see the [notebook on reading EDF files](importdata_edf.ipynb). However, the steps below show how to get data from any text-based format into `pypillometry`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "0d0f6616",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:36:18.351544Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:36:18.351227Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:36:19.195898Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:36:19.194823Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import pypillometry as pp\n",
    "from pypillometry import u\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6f527c61",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "In this example, we use data recorded with an Eyelink eyetracker. These eyetrackers store the data in binary files with the extension `.edf`. Some information about this file format is [here](http://download.sr-support.com/dispdoc/page25.html). We use a command-line utility released by Eyelink to convert this proprietary format into a more easily read `.asc` file that is a whitespace-separated plain-text format. The converter, `edf2asc`, can be downloaded for different platforms from the [Eyelink support forum](https://www.sr-research.com/support/). There is a GUI-based program for Windows and command-line programs for Linux and Mac. Binaries of the command-line tools for Linux and Mac are included in the `pypillometry` repository under [this link](https://github.com/ihrke/pypillometry/tree/master/external).\n",
    "\n",
    "On Linux, we call the program twice on an example EDF file, once for the samples and once for the events:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "5cd3d1f7",

   "source": [
    "This results in two files, one containing all the samples and one all the recorded events."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",

    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "fname_samples = \"../../data/test_samples.asc\"\n",
    "fname_events = \"../../data/test_events.asc\""
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e198da6d",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4dae7735",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We can read this file using `pandas.read_table()`. Eyelink marks missing x/y-coordinates with `\".\"` and missing pupil data with `0`. We convert both to `NaN`, which `pypillometry` treats as missing data. This is an explicit step: `pypillometry` does not interpret `0` as missing by itself."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "df = pd.read_table(fname_samples,\n",
    "                   names=[\"time\", \"left_x\", \"left_y\", \"left_p\",\n",
    "                          \"right_x\", \"right_y\", \"right_p\", \"flags\"],\n",
    "                   na_values=\".\", skipinitialspace=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Eyelink codes missing pupil data (e.g., blinks) as 0;\n",
    "# set it to NaN so that pypillometry treats it as missing\n",
    "df[\"left_p\"] = df.left_p.replace(0, np.nan)\n",
    "df[\"right_p\"] = df.right_p.replace(0, np.nan)\n",
    "df"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "64a5e76c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "After a header (lines starting with `**`) containing meta-information, we get a sequence of \"events\" which have different formats. We are interested in lines starting with \"MSG\" because those contain our experimental markers. Therefore, we read the events file and remove all rows that do not start with \"MSG\":"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "8a10381d",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.081890Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.081661Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.093040Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.092197Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "['MSG\\t2728855 DISPLAY_COORDS = 0 0 1919 1079\\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL Calibration points:  \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -29.4, -23.5        -0,     -2   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -29.3, -35.7        -0,  -1544   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -32.9, -10.4        -0,   1559   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -49.7, -23.0     -2835,     -2   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -10.8, -27.4      2835,     -2   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -48.3, -33.3     -2818,  -1544   \\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t2784000 !CAL -11.0, -34.2      2818,  -1544   \\n']"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 9,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# read the whole file into variable `events` (list with one entry per line)\n",
    "with open(fname_events) as f:\n",
    "    events = f.readlines()\n",
    "\n",
    "# keep only lines starting with \"MSG\"\n",
    "events = [ev for ev in events if ev.startswith(\"MSG\")]\n",
    "events[0:10]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "cd29ec19",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Our experiment sent a marker called `experiment_start` when the experiment started. Hence, we can remove all events before this marker."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "c21732d8",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.094982Z",

     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.098561Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.098069Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "['MSG\\t3387245 C_GW_1_1_UD_UD\\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t3390421 F_GW_1_1_10_0\\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t3392759 C_NW_1_2_UD_UD\\n',\n",
       " 'MSG\\t3394293 R_NW_1_2_UD_UD\\n',\n",

      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 10,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "experiment_start_index = np.where([\"experiment_start\" in ev for ev in events])[0][0]\n",
    "events = events[experiment_start_index+1:]\n",
    "events[0:10]"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "cda27d1e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Generalize to multiple similar datasets\n",
    "\n",
    "Now that we have found a way to create our `EyeData` object from the raw files, we can wrap the code from this notebook into a function that creates such objects for any file with the same structure.\n",
    "\n",
    "NOTE: You may want to consider using a [configuration file to facilitate loading and sharing your study data](../user_guide/studies.rst).\n",
    "\n",
    "The function takes the name of an EDF file as input, runs all the code above and returns the final `EyeData` object. For convenience, we assume that `edf2asc` has already been run so that the `.asc` files are available (see above)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 17,
   "id": "1475aeee",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.847165Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.846813Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.856031Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T13:36:29.854857Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "datapath = \"../../data\"  # this is where the data files are located\n",
    "\n",
    "def read_dataset(edffile):\n",
    "    basename = os.path.splitext(edffile)[0]  # remove .edf from filename\n",
    "    fname_samples = os.path.join(datapath, basename+\"_samples.asc\")\n",
    "    fname_events = os.path.join(datapath, basename+\"_events.asc\")\n",
    "    print(\"> Loading '%s' and '%s'\" % (fname_samples, fname_events))\n",
    "\n",
    "    # read samples file\n",
    "    df = pd.read_table(fname_samples,\n",
    "                       names=[\"time\", \"left_x\", \"left_y\", \"left_p\",\n",
    "                              \"right_x\", \"right_y\", \"right_p\", \"flags\"],\n",
    "                       na_values=\".\", skipinitialspace=True)\n",
    "    df[\"left_p\"] = df.left_p.replace(0, np.nan)\n",
    "    df[\"right_p\"] = df.right_p.replace(0, np.nan)\n",
    "\n",
    "    # read events file, keep only messages after the experiment started\n",
    "    with open(fname_events) as f:\n",
    "        events = [ev for ev in f.readlines() if ev.startswith(\"MSG\")]\n",
    "    experiment_start_index = np.where([\"experiment_start\" in ev for ev in events])[0][0]\n",
    "    events = events[experiment_start_index+1:]\n",
    "    df_ev = pd.Series(events).str.split(expand=True)\n",
    "    df_ev = df_ev[df_ev[4].isna()][[1, 2]]\n",
    "    df_ev.columns = [\"time\", \"event\"]\n",
    "\n",
    "    # create EyeData object\n",
    "    d = pp.EyeData(left_pupil=df.left_p, right_pupil=df.right_p,\n",
    "                   left_x=df.left_x, left_y=df.left_y,\n",
    "                   right_x=df.right_x, right_y=df.right_y,\n",
    "                   time=df.time,\n",
    "                   event_onsets=df_ev.time.astype(float), event_labels=df_ev.event,\n",
    "                   name=basename)\n",
    "    return d.reset_time()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "24d31014",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
